journeys.name: Punch in with optional Odoo project
journeys.population: US, UK, CA, NL, FR hourly; PL/DE where punch applies
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to start my shift with the right optional Odoo project and UKG labor categories so that my time is recorded in the right work context.
journeys.pre: Signed in through SSO and punched out. Odoo Project and Task / LOB may be left blank in the prototype; production project-requiredness remains open.
journeys.flow: 1. Open Punch while Out. 2. Optionally select an active assigned Odoo Project and Task / LOB. 3. Optionally use Add Transfer, or choose the home or a recent transfer in the transfer picker, to stage UKG labor categories. 4. Tap Punch In. 5. See a brief confirmation with the local time and project details when present.
journeys.alt: No active assigned Odoo projects -> leave Odoo fields blank in the prototype; production behavior depends on the project-requiredness decision. Already punched in -> Punch In is not offered.
journeys.rules: Odoo Project / Task / LOB and UKG Labor Category values are separate. No automatic mapping is implied. Project-requiredness remains open.
ac: I am punched out and may leave project fields blank
I tap Punch In
I see a confirmation with local time and project details when UKG accepts the punch
journeys.ev: Proposed - project-requiredness and integration remain open

journeys.name: Punch out to end the shift
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to punch out at the end of my shift so that my shift closes with an accurate total.
journeys.pre: Employee is punched in
journeys.flow: 1. Open Punch. 2. Review elapsed shift time. 3. Tap Punch Out. 4. See a brief confirmation with the action and local time.
journeys.alt: On break -> Punch Out also ends the break (break end recorded at the same time).
journeys.rules: Punch Out is only enabled while punched in. Shift total excludes unpaid break time. Prototype: elapsed shift time is not shown on the Punch screen yet.
ac: I am punched in
I tap Punch Out
an OUT punch is recorded and today's row on My Timecard shows the closed segment and daily total
I am punched out
I look at the Punch screen
Punch Out is disabled and Punch In is enabled
journeys.src: Global Time Entry UI/UX Specification §5.1.6; SRC-02, SRC-03, SRC-04, SRC-06, FSD TK-1

journeys.name: Start and end a break
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to record my meal break so that unpaid break time is excluded and break rules are met.
journeys.pre: Employee is punched in
journeys.flow: 1. Tap Start Break. 2. Status changes to On break; End Break is primary, Punch Out is secondary, and transfers are disabled. No live break timer is shown. 3. Tap End Break. 4. Work resumes on the same project.
journeys.alt: Break shorter than the configured minimum -> a Short break indicator on the affected My Timecard punch cell (TC-01). Country minimums and grace minutes remain open.
journeys.rules: Break start closes the current segment; break end opens a new segment on the same project and task. Paid/unpaid and minimum length are country rules.
ac: I am punched in on an optional Odoo project
I start and end an unpaid break
work resumes with the same project/task and the unpaid break is excluded from totals
my break lasted less than the configured minimum
the timecard is calculated
a Short break exception is shown on that day
journeys.src: Global Time Entry UI/UX Specification §5.1.4, §5.1.10; SRC-02, SRC-03, SRC-04, FSD TK-1

journeys.name: Stage or change UKG labor categories
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to stage or change UKG labor-category values so that my shift is charged to the right category.
journeys.pre: Employee is Out or In, not on break. UKG labor categories satisfy the configured eligibility and required-field rules; optional Odoo selection is separate.
journeys.flow: 1. The transfer picker shows the transfer in effect with its status (Next Punch In, or Since the time it started; no label when it is the home transfer); open it to choose the home transfer or a recent transfer, or tap Add Transfer. 2. Choose configured UKG labor-category levels in the Transfer drawer. 3. Review and confirm. 4. While Out, categories are staged for the next Punch In; while In, the transfer applies from that point forward.
journeys.alt: While on break, transfer controls are disabled until the break ends. Prototype: choosing the home transfer while Out clears a staged transfer; choosing the transfer already in effect changes nothing.
journeys.rules: UKG Labor Category Project, Task / LOB, Timecard Code, and Function are separate from Odoo Project and Task / LOB. Required levels and defaults remain open; no Odoo-to-UKG mapping is implied. The Transfer drawer omits Work Rule, Cost Center, and Business Structure.
ac: I am Out and choose Add Transfer
I confirm UKG labor categories
they are staged for my next Punch In without implying an Odoo mapping
I am In and choose Add Transfer
I confirm UKG labor categories
the transfer applies from that point forward
I am Out with a staged transfer
I choose the home transfer in the transfer picker
my next Punch In uses the home transfer and the picker shows no status label
journeys.ev: Proposed - labor-category profile and mapping remain open

journeys.name: Blocked punch for unassigned or inactive project
journeys.story: As Spiro Finance, I want punches blocked on projects that are closed or not assigned so that time is never charged to the wrong PRJ.
journeys.trigger: Employee selects or scans a project
journeys.pre: Odoo assignment sync has run
journeys.flow: 1. The employee selects an Odoo Project from the picker. 2. The picker offers active projects assigned to the employee. 3. Validate the selection again when Punch In is submitted. 4. If it became inactive or unassigned, do not record the punch and show a plain-language message.
journeys.alt: The Odoo Project is optional in the prototype and may be left blank. Whether production punches may start without a project remains open.
journeys.rules: Offer active assigned Odoo projects and revalidate the selected project at Punch In. Blank Odoo Project is allowed in the prototype. A deliberately blank selection is different from a selection that became inactive or unassigned: the latter must block recording with an explanation. UKG labor-category validation is separate. Revalidation is covered by automated model checks; production policy on blank project selection remains open.
journeys.api: None (CloudApper validation against Odoo assignment cache)
ac: I selected an assigned active Odoo project
it becomes inactive or unassigned before Punch In
the punch is blocked with an explanation; the selection is not silently converted to No project
journeys.ev: Confirmed - picker rule; production requiredness remains open
journeys.currentState: Prototype revalidates the selected project at Punch In and blocks unknown, inactive, unassigned or hidden selections. Deliberate No Project is allowed in the prototype. Automated model checks pass; production policy remains open.

journeys.name: Show actions for the current punch state
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to see the punch action available for my current state so that I can continue the punch flow.
journeys.pre: Current punch state known
journeys.flow: 1. Open Punch. 2. See actions for the current state: Out, In, or On break. 3. Choose an available action.
journeys.alt: UKG returns an error for a submitted punch -> show the error message returned by UKG.
journeys.rules: Out -> Punch In; In -> Transfer, Start Break, Punch Out; On break -> End Break, Punch Out. CloudApper sends a selected punch to UKG and displays any returned error, including duplicate-punch errors.
journeys.api: None for displaying the available actions; punch submissions are sent to UKG.
ac: I am punched in
I look at Punch
I see Transfer, Start Break, and Punch Out; Punch In is unavailable

journeys.name: See punch confirmation and UKG errors
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want clear feedback after a punch so that I know whether UKG accepted it.
journeys.trigger: A punch is sent to UKG
journeys.pre: Employee selects a Punch action
journeys.flow: 1. CloudApper sends the punch to UKG. 2. If UKG accepts it, show a brief confirmation with the action and local time. 3. Show the recorded event and available project, task, or labor-category details in Recent punches.
journeys.alt: UKG returns an error -> display the error message from UKG, including duplicate-punch errors.
journeys.rules: Show a success confirmation when UKG accepts the punch. If UKG returns an error, show the returned message to the employee. UKG transactions are simulated; success must follow simulated acceptance, and not precede it. Production contracts remain unverified.
journeys.api: POST /v1/timekeeping/timecard (punches.add; display the result returned by UKG)
ac: I submit a punch
UKG accepts it
I see a brief confirmation with the action and local time
journeys.currentState: Employee punch success and history updates follow simulated UKG acceptance. Buttons prevent repeat punch actions while the response is pending. Automated model checks pass; production UKG integration and full browser acceptance remain unverified.

journeys.name: Display an error returned by UKG
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to see an error returned by UKG when it cannot record my punch so that I know what happened.
journeys.pre: CloudApper has sent a punch to UKG
journeys.flow: 1. CloudApper sends the punch to UKG. 2. UKG returns an error. 3. CloudApper displays the error message returned by UKG, including duplicate-punch errors.
journeys.alt: UKG accepts the punch -> show a brief confirmation with the action and local time.
journeys.rules: Display the error returned by UKG to the employee.
ac: I send a punch to UKG
UKG returns a duplicate-punch error
I see the error message returned by UKG
demo: Punch > simulate a duplicate-punch error from UKG

journeys.name: Identify at a shared kiosk
journeys.story: As a warehouse employee without a company phone, I want to identify myself at a shared device so that I can punch without using my personal phone.
journeys.trigger: Employee arrives at the shared device
journeys.pre: Shared kiosk station available (shared-account provisioning remains open, §9); the employee's badge can be matched to a UKG person (production lookup remains open)
journeys.flow: 1. On the kiosk home, select Punch In, Punch Out, or Recent Punches. 2. Scan your badge; authentication is badge-only, with no employee number, username, or password. 3. After acceptance, the selected action is recorded, or your recent punches are shown. No employee details appear before acceptance. 4. The kiosk returns home after the result toast, Back or Cancel, or the 60-second countdown.
journeys.alt: Badge not recognised or invalid -> a clear error; nothing is recorded and the kiosk returns home. Barcode values are not shown in errors.
journeys.rules: Each action requires its own badge scan. Scan and history countdowns are 60 seconds. After returning home, no badge, employee identity, action, history, or detailed result stays visible apart from the brief result toast. Badge encoding, lookup, and authorization remain open (§9). Current source follows action-first badge-only scanning and 60-second countdowns. Production lookup/scanner/outage behavior is unverified; the invalid-badge error still includes the scanned value and must be corrected before production.
journeys.api: Badge -> person lookup (source to be confirmed)
ac: I am at the shared kiosk
I select Punch In and scan my badge
after acceptance I see a brief result toast with the action and local time, and the kiosk returns home
I select Recent Punches and scan my badge
I wait 60 seconds or tap Back
my history clears and the kiosk returns to its three-tile home screen
journeys.ev: Confirmed - user-approved kiosk flow (§5.5.1–5.5.4); production badge lookup and authorization remain open

journeys.name: Scan a job barcode to switch project (out of scope)
journeys.story: As a warehouse employee, I might want to scan a job barcode to change project. The spec requests no job or project barcode at the kiosk, so this journey is recorded only to show that decision.
journeys.trigger: Employee moves to a different job
journeys.pre: Not applicable: the kiosk requests no job or project barcode (§3.1, §5.5.2).
journeys.flow: Not in scope. Kiosk actions are Punch In, Punch Out, and Recent Punches after a badge scan (§5.5.1–5.5.2). No project or labor-category selection is included at the kiosk.
journeys.alt: None.
journeys.rules: Spec §3.1 and §5.5 request no job or project barcode.
ac: I am a kiosk user
I select Punch In
the kiosk asks me to scan my badge, not a job barcode
journeys.ev: Out of scope - no job or project barcode is requested by the current kiosk flow

journeys.name: Show, hide, or add Odoo projects for Punch
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to show, hide, or add the Odoo projects I work on so that the Punch project picker offers the right projects.
journeys.trigger: Employee needs a project that is not in the Punch picker
journeys.pre: Punched out. Odoo project assignments are available in the prototype's simulated catalog.
journeys.flow: 1. While Out, open the Project picker and choose Manage Odoo Project. 2. Show or hide assigned projects; hiding changes picker visibility only. 3. Choose Add projects from Odoo to see active projects not yet assigned. 4. Search by project name, client, or event and choose Add. The project becomes assigned, visible, and selected. 5. Choose Done, optionally choose its Task / LOB, and continue with Punch In.
journeys.alt: No matching projects -> explain the empty search result. Hidden projects remain assigned.
journeys.rules: Only active projects are offered. Showing or hiding does not remove an assignment. Odoo projects stay separate from UKG labor categories. Production catalog access, eligibility, assignment, and persistence remain open.
journeys.api: None in the prototype (simulated catalog); production Odoo catalog call remains open
ac: I am punched out and open the Project picker
I choose Manage Odoo Project, add a project from the catalog, and choose Done
the project is assigned, visible, and selected for my next Punch In
I hide an assigned project
I open the Project picker
the project is hidden from the picker but remains assigned
journeys.ev: Proposed - prototype; production catalog access, assignment, and persistence remain open
demo: Ava Mitchell > Punch > Project picker > Manage Odoo Project

journeys.name: Keep Odoo and UKG labor categories distinct
journeys.story: As an employee, I want optional Odoo project/task context and UKG labor categories clearly separated so that I understand what I am selecting without assuming an unapproved mapping.
journeys.trigger: Employee opens a punch or the weekly calendar
journeys.pre: Values available from Odoo or context
journeys.flow: 1. Choose an optional Odoo Project and Task / LOB where offered. 2. Select UKG labor categories separately through the Transfer drawer. 3. Do not assume one source prepopulates the other.
journeys.alt: No Odoo Project value is selected -> the employee may leave it blank in the prototype; production project-requiredness remains open.
journeys.rules: Odoo-to-UKG prefill mapping has not been selected. Source fields, mapping, precedence, overrides, refresh timing, and missing or inactive-value handling remain open.
ac: I open project or labor-category fields
I review their source
Odoo Project / Task and UKG labor categories remain separate unless a mapping is approved
demo: Ava Mitchell > Punch > Odoo project and labor category

journeys.name: Review my hourly timecard
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to review my punches, transfers and hours by day so that I can check my time for the selected period.
journeys.pre: Signed-in hourly employee; own timecard is available for the selected period. Salaried employees use Project Hours.
journeys.flow: 1. Open My Timecard from navigation or Recent punches. 2. Review employee, role, selected period dates and loaded time. 3. Review Date, In, Transfer (Project / Task / LOB), Out, Hours, Daily and Period. 4. Inspect read-only details and project/task totals below the grid.
journeys.alt: Breaks, transfers and split shifts create additional rows. Empty days have blank punch/hour cells and no Absence label; active segments show In progress and missing end punches show a read-only Missed punch label.
journeys.rules: My Timecard is for hourly employees only and is read-only. Edit, Comments, Add punch and correction actions are hidden and disabled. Schedule, Pay Code, Shift, separate Exceptions, Audit, UKG Sync and By Pay Code are omitted. Mobile scrolling stays inside the grid.
ac: I am an hourly employee viewing a selected period
I open My Timecard
the seven documented columns, header and project/task totals are shown in a read-only view
I view My Timecard
I review the grid and details
no edit, comment, add-punch or correction action is offered
journeys.currentState: Read-only. Edit and Comments are hidden and disabled, including in punch and transfer details. Adding, deleting, or correcting a punch and sending a correction request are unavailable; whether employees may edit punches is an open decision (TC-04).
gridFields: Show the date on the first row for that day. Keep the column compact on mobile.
Show the segment's recorded start time; open punch details without changing the time.
Keep the value on one line and truncate when needed. The details popover shows the full values.
Show the recorded end time. An active segment shows In progress; a missing end punch shows a read-only Missed punch label.
Show the worked hours for the segment, excluding unpaid breaks.
Show the day's total on its final row.
Show the running period total through that day.

journeys.name: Switch between pay periods
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to move between time periods so that I can review my recorded time.
journeys.pre: Current and previous period data are available.
journeys.flow: 1. Open My Timecard and read the displayed date range. 2. Select Previous to review the prior period. 3. Use Today or Next to return to the current period.
journeys.alt: At the available period boundary, the corresponding control is disabled. The prototype exposes only the current and previous periods.
journeys.rules: Navigation changes the date range, daily records and totals. Country pay-period rules remain open; all periods remain read-only.
ac: I view the current period
I select Previous
the previous period dates, records and totals appear
I view the previous period
I select Today or Next
the current period appears and Next is disabled at the current-period boundary
demo: Ava Mitchell > My Timecard > Previous / Today / Next

journeys.name: Open punch and transfer details
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to inspect punch times, labor category and transfer information so that I can verify what my timecard records.
journeys.trigger: Employee selects a recorded punch time or transfer
journeys.pre: The selected period contains a recorded In/Out punch or transfer.
journeys.flow: 1. Click, tap or right-click a recorded In/Out time or Transfer cell. 2. Review Date, Time and Punch type for a punch, or the full Project/Task allocation and time range for a transfer. 3. Review recorded UKG values in the separate Labor category group. 4. Close the popover, press Escape or click outside.
journeys.alt: When no labor category is recorded, the popover explains this. A truncated Transfer value is shown in full in its details.
journeys.rules: Details remain read-only and have no Edit or Comments actions. Transfer text stays on one line in the grid. Odoo Project/Task values remain separate from UKG labor categories.
ac: I review a recorded In or Out time
I open its details
Date, Time, Punch and recorded Labor category values appear without Edit or Comments
a Transfer value is truncated
I open its details
the full allocation and separate Labor category values are readable
demo: Ava Mitchell > My Timecard > select an In/Out time or Transfer

journeys.name: Employee punch editing is an open decision
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I may need to change a recorded In or Out time; whether employee editing will be enabled remains a decision for Spiro.
journeys.trigger: Employee spots an incorrect recorded punch time
journeys.pre: A recorded punch may need a correction; current My Timecard access is read-only.
journeys.flow: 1. Review My Timecard and the recorded punch details. 2. The current view provides no Edit or correction-request action. 3. Keep employee punch-edit access open until Spiro confirms Q-05.
journeys.alt: If editing is approved later, define eligible groups, editable periods, reasons, approval handling and direct-save versus Manager-review behavior.
journeys.rules: Punch editing is currently disabled and its controls are hidden. No correction-request route is assumed. Comments, missing-punch addition and employee approval are also unavailable in the current view.
journeys.api: No punch-update call is made from the current read-only view; a future update contract would need confirmation.

I review an incorrect or missing punch

journeys.name: Review totals by project and task
journeys.story: As an hourly employee, I want to review hours by project and task so that I can check how my time is allocated.
journeys.trigger: Employee reaches Totals below the timecard grid
journeys.pre: Punches and transfers are recorded in the selected period.
journeys.flow: 1. Review Totals below the timecard grid. 2. Review hours grouped by project and task. 3. Compare the period total with the running totals in the grid.
journeys.alt: No project hours in the period -> the totals table shows its empty state and a zero period total.
journeys.rules: The current view shows project/task totals only. By Pay Code, overtime and premium breakdowns are absent; future additions remain an open decision.
journeys.api: Calculated from the demo timecard segments; production totals source remains to be verified.

journeys.flow: 1. Open a new week. 2. See a row for each visible assigned project, with seven daily cells and a project total. 3. Use Projects or Manage projects to show or hide assignments; a hidden assignment remains available in Add new > All.
journeys.alt: Large project lists: a Copy & Archive fallback applies only if Q-13 confirms it. The project-count threshold is not yet set (GR-06).
journeys.rules: Odoo Project / Task / LOB and UKG labor-category values remain separate; no mapping is implied. Assignment source and details prefilled onto a row remain open.

journeys.name: Add a project row with quick lookup
journeys.story: As an employee on many PRJs, I want to search by PRJ number, client or show so that I find the right project fast.

journeys.alt: Project not in list -> contact PM (assignment missing).

I confirm Add new

journeys.name: Validate hours entered
journeys.story: As payroll, I want impossible values rejected so that bad data never reaches UKG.
journeys.flow: 1. Type a value. 2. Negative, non-numeric, more than 2 decimals, or a day over 24 hours is flagged at once. 3. Save is blocked until the errors are corrected.
journeys.rules: Nonnegative (zero allowed), at most 2 decimals, daily total <= 24. Only the current week is editable; adjacent weeks are read-only (§5.2.1). Comma or dot decimals accepted for EU locales.

journeys.alt: Copied project now closed -> row skipped with a note.

journeys.name: Land on the right time view for my population
journeys.story: As an employee, I want to open the app with SSO and land on the view that fits how I work so that I start right away.
journeys.pre: SSO configured; population attribute set
journeys.flow:

journeys.name: Review the current balance before submitting
journeys.story: As an employee, I want to see the selected request type balance on final review so that I can consider it before submitting.
journeys.pre: Balances synced from UKG
journeys.flow: 1. Choose a request type, dates, and duration. 2. On final review, see the current balance for that type with its unit and as-of time. 3. Do not show a projected balance or repeat it on confirmation.
journeys.alt: Current balance cannot be retrieved -> label it unavailable; never present an older balance as current.
journeys.rules: Show a balance only on the final review step before submission.

journeys.name: Request Time Off
journeys.story: As an employee, I want to request configured Time Off dates and duration so that the request can follow its documented status flow.
journeys.pre: Leave types configured
journeys.flow: 1. Choose an eligible request type. 2. Choose dates and a configured duration. Full Day uses an inclusive date range; Hours and both half-day durations use one date. 3. Add an optional note and review the request, including the current balance. 4. Submit once. 5. Show the request reference, dates, duration, and returned status: Submitted or a confirmed final status.
journeys.alt: Submission or status is uncertain -> preserve entered data and explain the next step without showing a false success.
journeys.rules: Show only configured eligible request types and durations. Do not repeat balance on confirmation. The policy matrix and eligibility remain open.

journeys.name: Date rules by leave type and region
journeys.story: As an employee, I want clear date rules so that I do not submit a request that will be refused.
journeys.pre: Regional leave-date rules configured
journeys.flow: 1. Choose a request type. 2. Select valid dates and a configured duration. 3. Allow past dates only for Sick Time; all other request types accept today or future dates.
journeys.alt: Country eligibility and request-period rules, including Sick Time lookback limits, remain open. Undefined-rule fallback behavior must be agreed rather than assumed.
journeys.rules: Full Day accepts an inclusive range. Hours, First Half Day, and Second Half Day each use one date. Any Sick Time lookback limit remains to be configured.

journeys.name: Track my request status
journeys.story: As an employee, I want to see my request status so that I know whether it was approved.
journeys.pre: Request exists
journeys.flow: 1. Open My requests. 2. See Approved, Refused, Submitted, or Cancelled, who needs to act next when known, and chronological status history or comments.
journeys.alt: Latest status cannot be confirmed -> keep the last confirmed status visible and show an update message with its last-updated time and offer Try again.
journeys.rules: Use the actual UKG Time Off request statuses as the request-status values: Approved, Refused, Submitted, and Cancelled. Do not substitute inferred statuses. Translate displayed labels into the selected language while preserving this status mapping.

journeys.name: Approve or refuse a managed employee request
journeys.story: As a Manager, I want to review requests for employees I manage so that I can make a clear Time Off decision.
journeys.pre: A Submitted request is in the Manager queue for an employee they manage.
journeys.flow: 1. Open Requests needing review in the CloudApper custom app and filter by status, employee, type, or date. 2. Review the employee, request, dates, units, note, deadline when applicable, and relevant history. 3. Confirm Approve or Refuse. 4. Enter a required reason before Refuse. 5. Save the decision and notify the employee with its result and timestamp.
journeys.alt: No assigned Manager -> exception handling is still open; do not introduce a new request status.
journeys.rules: Managers review only employees they manage. Only Submitted requests can be approved or refused. Refusal requires a reason saved to history and shared with the employee.
journeys.api: Time Off status sent to UKG

I try to confirm the decision

journeys.name: Automatically approve an eligible request after three days
journeys.story: As Spiro HR, I want an eligible request with no Manager decision after three days to become Approved so that the configured rule can complete it.
journeys.trigger: Three days pass after submission without a Manager decision
journeys.pre: The request remains Submitted and matches the configured eligibility rule.
journeys.flow: 1. Check the request against configured eligibility. 2. If it remains Submitted without a Manager decision for three days, set status to Approved. 3. Record the automatic decision, rule, and timestamp in history. 4. Notify the employee and remove it from the Manager review queue.
journeys.alt: Eligibility criteria, how the three days are counted, and exception routing remain open.
journeys.rules: Automatic approval is a CloudApper configuration rule. Keep the actual status Approved; do not create an Auto-approved status.
ac: a configured eligible request remains Submitted without a Manager decision for three days
the rule runs
the request becomes Approved and history records the rule and decision time
journeys.ev: Confirmed - three-day rule; eligibility and timing details remain open

journeys.name: Cancel a request only while it is Submitted
journeys.story: As an employee, I want to cancel my own Submitted request so that I can change plans.
journeys.pre: The request belongs to the employee and its current status is Submitted.
journeys.flow: 1. Open the request. 2. Choose Cancel. 3. After CloudApper confirms, show Cancelled and keep the request in history.
journeys.alt: Approved, Refused, or Cancelled request -> no employee cancel action is offered.
journeys.rules: Employees cannot edit a submitted request. Cancellation is available only for the employee's own Submitted request.

journeys.name: Recent punches at the kiosk
journeys.story: As a warehouse employee at a shared kiosk, I want to see my recent punches so that I can check what was recorded.
journeys.trigger: Employee checks recent punches at the kiosk
journeys.pre: Kiosk station available. The badge can be matched to a UKG person (production lookup remains open).
journeys.flow: 1. On the kiosk home, select Recent Punches. 2. Scan your badge; authentication is badge-only. 3. The history shows up to six latest events, newest first, with the label, local time and date, and project detail when applicable. 4. Back, or the 60-second countdown, returns home and clears the history.
journeys.alt: Badge not recognised or invalid -> a clear error with no history, and the kiosk returns home. No events -> an empty-state message.
journeys.rules: Up to six events, newest first. No employee name, badge verified banner, or footer. The history clears on return home. Current source follows action-first badge-only scanning and 60-second countdowns. Production lookup/scanner/outage behavior is unverified; the invalid-badge error still includes the scanned value and must be corrected before production.
journeys.api: Badge -> person lookup (source to be confirmed); punch history read (to be confirmed)
ac: I select Recent Punches on the kiosk
I scan my badge
I see up to six events, newest first, with no employee name
I select Recent Punches on the kiosk
I wait 60 seconds or tap Back
the history clears and the kiosk returns home
journeys.ev: Confirmed - user-approved kiosk flow (§5.5.3); production lookup remains open

journeys.name: Kiosk timeout, cancel, and return home
journeys.story: As a warehouse employee at a shared kiosk, I want the kiosk to clear my information after a timeout so that the next person does not see my details.
journeys.trigger: Employee leaves the kiosk or the scan is not completed
journeys.pre: A scan or history screen is open on the kiosk.
journeys.flow: 1. The scan screen shows a 60-second countdown. 2. Back or Cancel clears the action and returns home at once. 3. If the countdown ends, the action is cleared, the kiosk explains the timeout, and it returns home. 4. The history clears after its 60-second countdown and returns home without a message.
journeys.alt: After a recorded punch, the brief result toast appears and the kiosk returns home.
journeys.rules: Leave no badge, employee identity, action, history, or detailed result visible after returning home, apart from the brief result toast. The 60-second scan/history timeout is approved; production outage handling remains open. Current source follows action-first badge-only scanning and 60-second countdowns. Production lookup/scanner/outage behavior is unverified; the invalid-badge error still includes the scanned value and must be corrected before production.
ac: I start Punch In on the kiosk
I wait 60 seconds without scanning
the action is cleared, the timeout is explained, and the kiosk returns home
I start Punch In on the kiosk
I tap Back or Cancel on the scan screen
the action clears at once and the kiosk returns home
journeys.ev: Confirmed - user-approved kiosk flow (§5.5.4); outage handling remains open

questions.question: Will hourly employees be allowed to change recorded In/Out punches? If yes, confirm eligible groups, editable periods, required reasons, approval handling, and whether changes save directly or require Manager review.
questions.why: Determines whether a future employee punch-edit journey is enabled. My Timecard remains read-only, with editing disabled and controls hidden until the decision is confirmed; no correction-request route is assumed (spec §§5.1.10, 9).

questions.question: Which labor-category profiles will be used for the employee population?
questions.why: Determines the labor-category fields available to each employee population.

questions.question: Which Odoo projects can employees see and select, who assigns them (employee, Manager, or automatically from Odoo), and are added or hidden projects saved? May employees add projects themselves?
questions.why: Defines project access, assignment permissions, and persistence of picker visibility.

questions.question: Whether and how should Odoo Project / Task populate UKG Project, Task / LOB, Timecard Code, or Function for punches, transfers, and project hours? Define source fields, mapping, precedence/defaults, overrides, refresh, required levels, and missing/inactive/unassigned handling. Confirm UKG payloads against journey-register Q-12.
questions.why: No mapping is chosen. Odoo and UKG fields remain separate, and Transfer uses manual selection until this is resolved.

questions.question: Which UKG field identifies hourly or salaried employees? What happens when it is missing or unclear? Does type alone select Punch versus weekly project hours, or are there exceptions such as the Poland transition group?
questions.why: Defines landing-view routing and the fallback for incomplete employee records.

questions.question: How should approval of hourly project time work, and what must CloudApper do to support it?
questions.why: Confirmed: salaried project hours need no approval; exceeding estimated project time does not itself require approval.

questions.question: Which duration types should each Time Off request type support: Full Day, Hours, First Half Day, or Second Half Day? Also confirm eligible types/subtypes, Sick Time lookback, regional eligibility/request-period rules, required questions/documents and unavailable-balance behavior.
questions.why: Defines the request-type duration matrix. Linked journeys are now included in Journeys.

questions.question: Should only the employee's direct Manager approve or refuse Time Off requests, or should the manager's manager also be able to act?
questions.why: Defines who may review requests. New question ID assigned for this spec decision; linked journeys are now included in Journeys.

questions.question: Define auto-approval eligibility, calendar/working-day counting, notification channels, and handling of requests without an assigned Manager.
questions.why: Confirmed: employee notes optional; managed employees' Managers review; refusal reason required; no employee editing; only Submitted requests may be cancelled. Team availability planning is excluded. Linked journeys are now included in Journeys.

questions.question: Confirm badge provisioning/encoding, lookup/authorization, scanners, timekeeping endpoint/timestamps, duplicate handling, and outage recovery. How will shared kiosk accounts be provisioned?
questions.why: Shared-account provisioning remains open. Action-first scanning, tiles, 60-second timeouts, and result feedback are approved.

questions.question: Should badges be read with the device camera or a USB barcode scanner? Confirm the device to be used.
questions.why: Determines production kiosk hardware and badge input.

questions.question: Must every hourly employee punch include a project from Odoo?
questions.why: Determines project-requiredness and whether a punch may proceed without an Odoo project.

questions.question: May employees change project hours after they are saved? May they edit only the current week or earlier weeks, and how far back?
questions.why: Defines saved-entry edit permissions and the allowed edit period.

questions.question: Confirm the attached-scanner badge input: encoding, scan timing, and invalid-scan handling. The kiosk requests no job or project barcode (§3.1, §5.5).

Define and approve the project dashboard audience, measures, layout, thresholds and data freshness. The demo's Home project-budget panels are illustrative; dashboard requirements and design remain subject to review.
questions.why: Align the illustrative Home panels with agreed reporting requirements before treating them as accepted scope.

questions.question: Is a note mandatory when rejecting project time? (It is required for Time Off.)
Which teams get Copy and Archive instead of auto-population, and what is the project-count threshold?
Confirm corrected Cerulean hex value in the Brand Guidelines and approve semantic UI color tokens.
